summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic pancreatitis, portal hypertension, esophageal varices, and asthma was admitted for worsening epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, and blood-streaked emesis following a relapse in alcohol use. He had been consuming two pints of brandy daily for two weeks and reported drinking to alleviate pain and withdrawal symptoms, including tremors and visual hallucinations. Initial labs showed elevated alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, and hypernatremia, with a positive serum ethanol level. Imaging confirmed cirrhosis with portal hypertension and splenomegaly. He was treated for presumed alcoholic hepatitis and chronic pancreatitis with pain control, IV fluids, and symptom management. Alcohol withdrawal was monitored with CIWA, and he received Ativan as needed. Asthma was managed with a prednisone taper and inhalers. His condition improved, with stable vital signs, improved labs, and reduced pain. He was discharged home on his baseline medications, including nadolol, spironolactone, omeprazole, and lactulose, with a short prednisone course and follow-up arranged with primary care and addiction services.
